segments.source: The shortlist is for a US buyer with no convenient outlet at the espresso station. The brewer must operate without its own electric pump or heater, have a currently identifiable US configuration, and solve a different workflow. We selected the current Flair Classic kit with two portafilters and the 9Barista Mk.2 Standard configured for the buyer’s stove. Both have existing Coffeedant full reviews. We excluded plug-in manual levers such as an electrically heated Flair 58 and did not treat every moka pot as an espresso maker. [1] [3]
segments.context: The shortlist is for a US buyer with no convenient outlet at the espresso station. The brewer must operate without its own electric pump or heater, have a currently identifiable US configuration, and solve a different workflow. We selected the current Flair Classic kit with two portafilters and the 9Barista Mk.2 Standard configured for the buyer’s stove. Both have existing Coffeedant full reviews. We excluded plug-in manual levers such as an electrically heated Flair 58 and did not treat every moka pot as an espresso maker. [1] [3]

segments.source: Neither choice makes a whole setup powerless by itself. The Flair needs separately heated water. The 9Barista needs a compatible burner or stove; an electric stove still consumes power, just away from the brewer body. Both require a separate milk method. This distinction matters more than a marketing claim of “no electricity.”

segments.source: Flair says the Classic needs boiled water and includes a Flow Control portafilter plus a Bottomless 2-in-1 portafilter in the current kit. The restricted-flow option lowers the grinder threshold; the bottomless option calls for espresso-fine adjustment and fresh coffee. The direct lever and gauge put pressure timing in your hands. Older Classic reviews may describe a different bundle, so check the current box list. [1] [2] [5]

segments.source: 9Barista sells the Mk.2 in Standard and Pro configurations and asks buyers to select their stove type. The machine body is the same across induction and non-induction options, but the supplied heat plate differs. This guide covers Standard; Pro basket and portafilter claims do not apply to it. A 9Barista is a hot metal vessel after brewing. Let it cool and follow its instructions before disassembly. [3]
